title: Identity safety & crypto acceptance orchestration and signoff criteria
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This ticket captures the product acceptance orchestration for identity, authorization, and cryptographic controls required for Private/VPC deployments. It consolidates SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning expectations, RBAC model clarity, immutable audit logging requirements, and KMS/HSM key lifecycle controls into a single sign-off flow for customer-facing private deployments. The goal is to produce a deterministic checklist and test plan that SRE, Security, QA, and Solutions Engineering can run to declare a deployment "production-ready" for enterprise customers with strict compliance needs.
scope: In-scope: SAML 2.0 SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, OIDC basic flows for first-party apps, SCIM v2 provisioning, RBAC role templates and grant flows, immutable audit events for authn/authz/key ops, KMS BYOK import and key rotation, HSM-backed key usage for signing and encryption. Out-of-scope for this ticket: full airgap installer verification, FIPS validation, third-party HSM integration beyond our reference HSM solution.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: Customer can configure SAML IdP metadata and perform both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logins using a reference IdP; SAML assertions are validated for signature, audience, and conditions; automated tests exercise SAML logout and session expiration behavior.
SSO: OIDC flows for Redwood Console service-to-service auth complete with token introspection and refresh; tokens include expected claims and scopes in staging and prod-like environments.

Provisioning: SCIM v2 endpoints accept create/update/delete and return RFC-compliant responses; provisioning delta tests cover user->group mapping and attribute sync; downstream RBAC updates propagate within defined SLA (<=60s) in test harness.

RBAC: Role templates (Viewer, Editor, Admin, Org-Admin) exist and map to documented model; policy simulator produces expected allow/deny outcomes for representative resources; delegated admin flows are covered by unit and integration tests.

Audit logs: Authn/authz/KMS/HSM events are emitted to the configured audit sink with stable schema (timestamp, user_id, actor_type, action, resource, result, request_id, origin_ip); sample logs are produced and ingested into the audit pipeline in test infra.

KMS/HSM: BYOK import path validated (key import, label metadata, retention policy); key rotation executed end-to-end with no data-loss scenario; HSM signing and AES envelope encryption operations succeed and are logged; split-knowledge operator workflows documented and simulation run.
Security controls: Administrative UI requires MFA for high-priv actions; ephemeral operator sessions are time-limited and audited; RBAC privilege elevation requires approval workflow test coverage.
Failure and fallback: In case of KMS unavailability, defined fallback behavior used (fail-safe mode or degraded operation) is exercised in chaos test and documented in runbook.
Documentation & artifacts: Customer-facing admin guide, operator runbook, and SAML/SCIM metadata examples reviewed and published; test runbook and sample logs attached to the ticket.
Signoff: Security review OK, QA regression tests green, SRE smoke checklist passed in staging, Solutions Eng acceptance for customer onboarding scenarios.
decisions: Include SCIM v2 provisioning in scope after customer pilot feedback (decision 2025-01-20).
Require immutable audit schema with request_id and origin_ip; dropped older free-form log format for consistency (decision 2025-01-28).
Adopt BYOK as default KMS flow for enterprise Private deployments; provide optional operator-managed HSM for high-compliance customers (decision 2025-01-30).
open_questions: Do we require encrypted assertions for all customer IdPs or only for those with regulatory needs? Owner: Security.
What SLA should we guarantee for SCIM provisioning latency in Dedicated vs Private? Owner: PM + SRE.
Do we accept third-party HSM attestation reports (vendor-signed) in lieu of on-prem HSM QA? Owner: Legal + Security.
Should audit retention defaults be 1 year or configurable per-customer at creation? Owner: Product.
What is the minimum acceptable KMS rotation frequency we will require for signoff? Owner: Security.
Is a manual emergency key-rotation runbook required to be tested in every release? Owner: SRE.
signoff_steps: PM review and confirm acceptance criteria coverage
Security engineering review and threat-model signoff
SRE runbook validation and chaos test pass
QA full regression and smoke pass in staging
Legal review for BYOK and export controls where applicable
Final cross-team signoff meeting and ticket closure
notes: This ticket merges prior discrete checklists into a single orchestrated signoff. Keep communication tight with Solutions Eng during pilot onboarding. If any critical regression is found during SRE chaos testing, escalate to on-call infra lead and pause signoffs until RCA is completed. The artifacts listed should be attached to the ticket before requesting final signoff meeting.
